description: A server-side HTTP endpoint defined in a route.ts file using Web-standard Request and Response objects.
An exported async function named GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE in route.ts that handles matching HTTP method requests.
The standard Web API accessed via new URL(request.url).searchParams to read query string filters safely.
The App Router constraint prohibiting page.tsx and route.ts from living in the same route folder because both claim the same URL.
The architectural split between UI-bound React form mutations using Server Actions and public HTTP APIs or webhooks using Route Handlers.
